abstract.explanation: Marks a class as incomplete or a member as requiring implementation in a derived class.
abstract.example: abstract class Shape { public abstract double Area(); }

as.explanation: Safely converts a value to a compatible reference or nullable type, returning null if the conversion fails.
as.example:
object value = "hi";
string text = value as string;

base.explanation: Refers to the base class, usually to call a base constructor or overridden member.
base.example: class Dog : Animal { public Dog(string name) : base(name) {} }

break.explanation: Exits the nearest loop or switch statement immediately.
break.example: for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { if (i == 3) break; }

case.explanation: Defines a matching branch inside a switch statement or switch expression.

catch.explanation: Handles an exception thrown by a matching try block.

checked.explanation: Enables overflow checking for arithmetic operations and conversions.

class.explanation: Defines a reference type blueprint for objects with fields, properties, methods, and events.
class.example: class User { public string Name { get; set; } = "Nina"; }

const.explanation: Declares a compile-time constant whose value cannot change.

continue.explanation: Skips the rest of the current loop iteration and moves to the next one.
continue.example: for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if (i == 2) continue; Console.WriteLine(i); }

default.explanation: Gets the default value of a type, or labels the fallback branch in a switch.
default.example:
int n = default;
switch (n) { default: Console.WriteLine("Other"); break; }

delegate.explanation: Defines a type-safe reference to a method with a specific signature.
delegate.example:
delegate int MathOp(int a, int b);
MathOp add = (a, b) => a + b;

do.explanation: Starts a do-while loop, which runs the body before checking the condition.

else.explanation: Runs code when a previous if or else-if condition is false.

enum.explanation: Defines a named set of constant values.
enum.example:
enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }
Color c = Color.Green;

event.explanation: Declares a member that other code can subscribe to and unsubscribe from.

explicit.explanation: Declares a conversion operator that requires an explicit cast.
explicit.example: public static explicit operator int(User u) => u.Id;

extern.explanation: Declares a method implemented outside the C# source, often in native code.

finally.explanation: Runs after try/catch whether or not an exception occurred, commonly for cleanup.

fixed.explanation: Pins a movable variable so the garbage collector cannot relocate it during unsafe pointer work.

for.explanation: Repeats a block using an initializer, condition, and iterator.

foreach.explanation: Iterates through every item in a collection or array.

goto.explanation: Jumps to a labeled statement, case label, or default label.

if.explanation: Runs a block only when a condition is true.

implicit.explanation: Declares a conversion operator that can run automatically without a cast.
implicit.example: public static implicit operator string(User u) => u.Name;

in.explanation: Marks a parameter as passed by readonly reference, or appears in foreach and query syntax.
in.example:
void Print(in int value) { Console.WriteLine(value); }
foreach (var item in items) { }

interface.explanation: Declares a contract of members that implementing types must provide.

internal.explanation: Makes a type or member accessible only inside the same assembly/project.

is.explanation: Tests whether a value is compatible with a type or pattern.

lock.explanation: Acquires a mutual-exclusion lock to protect a critical section from concurrent access.

namespace.explanation: Groups related types under a named container and avoids naming collisions.

new.explanation: Creates an instance, hides an inherited member, or constrains generics to types with a public parameterless constructor.

operator.explanation: Declares a custom operator overload for a user-defined type.
operator.example: public static Point operator +(Point a, Point b) => new(a.X + b.X, a.Y + b.Y);

out.explanation: Marks a parameter assigned by the called method, or appears in generic variance.

override.explanation: Replaces a virtual, abstract, or override member inherited from a base class.

params.explanation: Allows a method to accept a variable number of arguments as an array.

private.explanation: Makes a member accessible only inside the containing type.

protected.explanation: Makes a member accessible inside the containing type and derived types.

public.explanation: Makes a type or member accessible from any code that can reference it.
public.example: public class User { public string Name { get; set; } = ""; }

readonly.explanation: Prevents reassignment of a field after construction, or marks members/structs as not mutating state.
readonly.example:
readonly int id;
public User(int id) { this.id = id; }

ref.explanation: Passes a variable by reference so the called method can read and assign the caller's variable.

return.explanation: Exits a method and optionally returns a value.
return.example: int Square(int x) { return x * x; }

sealed.explanation: Prevents a class from being inherited, or prevents an override from being overridden again.

sizeof.explanation: Returns the size in bytes of an unmanaged type.

stackalloc.explanation: Allocates a block of memory on the stack.

static.explanation: Marks a member as belonging to the type itself instead of an instance, or declares a static type/member.
static.example:
static int Count;
static void Print() { }

struct.explanation: Defines a value type, usually for small data structures.
struct.example: struct Point { public int X; public int Y; }

switch.explanation: Selects one branch from multiple possible cases using statements or expressions.

this.explanation: Refers to the current instance of a type.

throw.explanation: Raises an exception or rethrows the current exception.

try.explanation: Starts a block where exceptions can be caught or cleaned up with finally.

typeof.explanation: Gets the System.Type object that represents a type.

unchecked.explanation: Disables overflow checking for arithmetic operations and conversions.

unsafe.explanation: Allows pointer operations and other unsafe code inside a block, member, or type.

using.explanation: Imports a namespace/type, creates an alias, or disposes a resource at the end of a scope.
using.example:
using System;
using var reader = File.OpenText("data.txt");

virtual.explanation: Allows a member to be overridden in a derived class.

volatile.explanation: Indicates that a field can be modified by multiple threads and should not be aggressively optimized.

while.explanation: Repeats a block while a condition remains true.

bool.explanation: Represents true/false Boolean values. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

byte.explanation: Represents an unsigned 8-bit integer from 0 to 255. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

sbyte.explanation: Represents a signed 8-bit integer from -128 to 127. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

char.explanation: Represents a single UTF-16 character. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

decimal.explanation: Represents a high-precision decimal number, commonly used for money. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

double.explanation: Represents a double-precision floating-point number. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

float.explanation: Represents a single-precision floating-point number. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

int.explanation: Represents a signed 32-bit integer. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

uint.explanation: Represents an unsigned 32-bit integer. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

long.explanation: Represents a signed 64-bit integer. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

ulong.explanation: Represents an unsigned 64-bit integer. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

short.explanation: Represents a signed 16-bit integer. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

ushort.explanation: Represents an unsigned 16-bit integer. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

object.explanation: The base type of all C# types. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

string.explanation: Represents text as a sequence of characters. It is also a reserved C# keyword and aliases System.String.

void.explanation: Used as a method return type to say the method returns no value. It is also a reserved C# keyword.

true.explanation: Boolean literal representing the value true.

false.explanation: Boolean literal representing the value false.

null.explanation: Represents the absence of an object reference or nullable value.

add.explanation: Defines a custom event subscription accessor.
add.example: event EventHandler Clicked { add { handlers += value; } remove { handlers -= value; } }

allows.explanation: Used in newer generic constraint syntax to permit specific anti-constraints.
allows.example: class Box<T> where T : allows ref struct { }

alias.explanation: Used with extern alias to reference types from assemblies with the same fully qualified names.

ascending.explanation: Specifies ascending order in a LINQ query expression.
ascending.example: var q = from n in nums orderby n ascending select n;

args.explanation: Represents command-line arguments in top-level statements.

async.explanation: Marks a method, lambda, or anonymous method as asynchronous so it can use await.
async.example: async Task<string> LoadAsync() { return await GetTextAsync(); }

await.explanation: Suspends an async method until an awaitable operation completes.

by.explanation: Specifies the grouping key in a LINQ group clause.
by.example: var q = from p in people group p by p.City;

closed.explanation: Contextual keyword listed for newer/preview C# syntax; use only when the selected language version supports it.
closed.example: /* Preview contextual keyword; exact syntax depends on the enabled C# language version. */

Cdecl.explanation: Specifies the Cdecl unmanaged calling convention for function pointers.

descending.explanation: Specifies descending order in a LINQ query expression.
descending.example: var q = from n in nums orderby n descending select n;

dynamic.explanation: Defers member binding to runtime instead of compile time.

equals.explanation: Specifies equality comparison in a LINQ join clause.
equals.example: var q = from a in authors join b in books on a.Id equals b.AuthorId select b;

extension.explanation: Contextual keyword used by newer/preview C# extension-member syntax.
extension.example: /* Preview contextual keyword; exact syntax depends on the enabled C# language version. */

Fastcall.explanation: Specifies the Fastcall unmanaged calling convention for function pointers.

field.explanation: Accesses the compiler-generated backing field inside a property accessor in newer C# versions.
field.example: public int Age { get; set => field = value >= 0 ? value : throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(); }

file.explanation: Restricts a top-level type so it is visible only within the current source file.

from.explanation: Starts a LINQ query expression and introduces a range variable.
from.example: var q = from n in nums where n > 0 select n;

get.explanation: Defines a property or indexer getter accessor.

global.explanation: Qualifies the global namespace or declares a global using directive.
global.example:
global using System;
var text = global::System.String.Empty;

group.explanation: Groups LINQ query results by a key.
group.example: var q = from p in people group p by p.City;

init.explanation: Defines an init-only property setter that can be assigned during object initialization.

into.explanation: Introduces a continuation identifier in LINQ query syntax.
into.example: var q = from n in nums group n by n % 2 into g select g;

join.explanation: Joins two data sources in a LINQ query expression.
join.example: var q = from a in authors join b in books on a.Id equals b.AuthorId select b;

let.explanation: Introduces a temporary range variable inside a LINQ query.
let.example: var q = from s in names let len = s.Length where len > 3 select s;

managed.explanation: Specifies a managed function pointer calling convention.

nameof.explanation: Returns the name of a variable, type, or member as a string.

nint.explanation: Represents a signed native-sized integer. It is a contextual keyword and predefined type.

not.explanation: Negates a pattern in pattern matching.

notnull.explanation: Generic constraint requiring a type argument to be non-nullable.

nuint.explanation: Represents an unsigned native-sized integer. It is a contextual keyword and predefined type.

on.explanation: Specifies the left key in a LINQ join clause.
on.example: var q = from a in authors join b in books on a.Id equals b.AuthorId select b;

orderby.explanation: Sorts query results in LINQ query syntax.
orderby.example: var q = from n in nums orderby n select n;

partial.explanation: Splits a type or member declaration across multiple files or declarations.
partial.example:
partial class User { }
partial class User { }

record.explanation: Declares a reference or value type with value-based equality and concise data syntax.

remove.explanation: Defines a custom event unsubscription accessor.
remove.example: event EventHandler Clicked { add { handlers += value; } remove { handlers -= value; } }

required.explanation: Requires a property or field to be initialized by an object initializer or constructor.
required.example: class User { public required string Name { get; init; } }

safe.explanation: Contextual keyword listed for newer/preview C# syntax; use only when the selected language version supports it.
safe.example: /* Preview contextual keyword; exact syntax depends on the enabled C# language version. */

scoped.explanation: Restricts the lifetime of a ref-safe value so it cannot escape its scope.

select.explanation: Projects the result shape in a LINQ query expression.
select.example: var q = from n in nums select n * 2;

set.explanation: Defines a property or indexer setter accessor.

Stdcall.explanation: Specifies the Stdcall unmanaged calling convention for function pointers.

Thiscall.explanation: Specifies the Thiscall unmanaged calling convention for function pointers.

unmanaged.explanation: Used as a generic constraint for unmanaged types or as a function pointer calling convention context.

value.explanation: Represents the assigned value inside a property/indexer setter or event accessor.
value.example:
private string name = "";
public string Name { set { name = value; } }

var.explanation: Lets the compiler infer the type of a local variable from its initializer.

when.explanation: Adds a condition to a catch clause or switch case/pattern.

where.explanation: Adds a generic type constraint or filters results in a LINQ query.
where.example:
class Box<T> where T : class { }
var q = from n in nums where n > 0 select n;

with.explanation: Creates a copy of a record or struct with selected properties changed.

yield.explanation: Returns items one at a time from an iterator method.
yield.example: IEnumerable<int> Count() { yield return 1; yield return 2; }

System.explanation: The root .NET namespace containing fundamental types such as Console, Math, DateTime, String, Object, and Exception.

System.Console.explanation: Provides standard input, output, and error streams for console applications.

Console.explanation: The commonly used class for reading from and writing to the console, usually imported from System.

System.Math.explanation: Provides mathematical constants and static methods.

Math.explanation: Common shorthand for System.Math when System is imported.

System.String.explanation: The .NET type behind the C# string keyword.

String.explanation: The .NET class for text; equivalent to the C# string alias when System is imported.

System.Object.explanation: The .NET base type behind the C# object keyword.

Object.explanation: The base class for all .NET types; equivalent to the C# object alias when System is imported.

System.Boolean.explanation: The .NET type behind the C# bool keyword.

System.Int32.explanation: The .NET type behind the C# int keyword.

System.Double.explanation: The .NET type behind the C# double keyword.

System.Decimal.explanation: The .NET type behind the C# decimal keyword.

System.DateTime.explanation: Represents a date and time value.

DateTime.explanation: Common shorthand for System.DateTime when System is imported.

System.TimeSpan.explanation: Represents a duration or time interval.

TimeSpan.explanation: Common shorthand for System.TimeSpan when System is imported.

Guid.explanation: Common shorthand for System.Guid when System is imported.

System.Exception.explanation: The base class for runtime errors that can be thrown and caught.

Exception.explanation: Common shorthand for System.Exception when System is imported.

System.ArgumentException.explanation: Exception used when a method receives an invalid argument.

System.InvalidOperationException.explanation: Exception used when an object is in the wrong state for an operation.

System.IDisposable.explanation: Interface for objects that release resources through Dispose().

IDisposable.explanation: Common shorthand for System.IDisposable when System is imported.

System.Array.explanation: The base class for all arrays in .NET.

Array.explanation: Common shorthand for System.Array when System is imported.

System.Random.example:
Random rng = new Random();
int n = rng.Next(1, 10);

Random.explanation: Common shorthand for System.Random when System is imported.

System.Collections.explanation: Contains non-generic collection types such as ArrayList and Hashtable.

System.Collections.Generic.explanation: Contains strongly typed generic collection interfaces and classes such as List<T> and Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.

List.explanation: A strongly typed resizable list of items, usually used as List<T>.

Dictionary.explanation: A key/value collection, usually used as Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.

HashSet.explanation: A collection of unique values, usually used as HashSet<T>.

Queue.explanation: A first-in, first-out collection, usually used as Queue<T>.

Stack.explanation: A last-in, first-out collection, usually used as Stack<T>.

IEnumerable.explanation: Represents a sequence that can be iterated with foreach, usually as IEnumerable<T>.

ICollection.explanation: Represents a collection of items, usually as ICollection<T>.

IList.explanation: Represents an indexable list, usually as IList<T>.

System.Linq.explanation: Contains LINQ extension methods for querying and transforming sequences.
System.Linq.example:
using System.Linq;
var evens = nums.Where(n => n % 2 == 0);

LINQ.explanation: Language Integrated Query: C# query syntax plus extension methods for filtering, projecting, grouping, and transforming data.

Where.explanation: Filters a sequence using a condition.

Select.explanation: Projects each item in a sequence into a new form.

OrderBy.explanation: Sorts a sequence in ascending order by a key.

GroupBy.explanation: Groups items in a sequence by a key.

ToList.explanation: Creates a List<T> from a sequence.

FirstOrDefault.explanation: Returns the first matching item or the default value if none exists.

System.IO.explanation: Contains types for reading and writing files, directories, and streams.

File.explanation: Provides static methods for creating, reading, writing, and deleting files.

Directory.explanation: Provides static methods for working with directories.

Stream.explanation: Base type for reading and writing byte streams.

FileStream.explanation: Represents a stream backed by a file.

System.Text.explanation: Contains types for text processing and encoding.
System.Text.example:
using System.Text;
var sb = new StringBuilder();

StringBuilder.explanation: Builds strings efficiently through repeated appends or modifications.

System.Text.Json.explanation: Contains APIs for JSON serialization and deserialization.

JsonSerializer.explanation: Serializes objects to JSON and deserializes JSON into objects.

System.Threading.explanation: Contains types for threading, synchronization, and cancellation.

Task<T>.explanation: Represents an asynchronous operation that returns a value.

CancellationToken.explanation: Signals cancellation to async or long-running operations.

System.Net.Http.explanation: Contains HTTP client APIs for sending requests and receiving responses.
System.Net.Http.example:
using System.Net.Http;
var client = new HttpClient();

HttpClient.explanation: Sends HTTP requests and receives HTTP responses.
HttpClient.example:
using var client = new HttpClient();
string html = await client.GetStringAsync(url);

System.Reflection.explanation: Contains APIs for inspecting assemblies, types, and members at runtime.

System.Diagnostics.explanation: Contains types for diagnostics, tracing, processes, and debugging.

#if.explanation: Conditionally includes code when a symbol expression is true.

#else.explanation: Provides the alternative branch for a preprocessor conditional.

#elif.explanation: Adds an else-if branch to a preprocessor conditional.

#define.explanation: Defines a conditional compilation symbol for the current file.

#undef.explanation: Undefines a conditional compilation symbol for the current file.

#error.example: #error This build target is not supported

#line.explanation: Changes the compiler's reported line number or file name.

#region.explanation: Starts a collapsible region in editors.

#pragma.explanation: Gives special instructions to the compiler, commonly to enable or disable warnings.

#nullable.explanation: Controls nullable reference type warnings and annotations.

==.explanation: Compares two values. For strings C# compares the TEXT, which is different from Java - but for your own classes it compares identity unless the class says otherwise.

%.explanation: Remainder (modulo): what is left over after division. n % 2 == 0 means n is even.

/.explanation: Division. Between two INTEGERS the remainder is thrown away: 7 / 2 is 3. Make one side a double to get a decimal.

++.explanation: Adds one to a variable, in place.

+=.explanation: Adds to a variable and stores the result back in it.

&&.explanation: Logical AND: true only when both sides are true. Stops at the first false side.

||.explanation: Logical OR: true when either side is true.

??.explanation: Null coalescing: use the right side only when the left is null.

?..explanation: Null-conditional: read a member only if the object is not null, instead of throwing.

=>.explanation: Lambda, or an expression-bodied member: a short way to write a function or a property.

=.explanation: Assignment: puts the value on the right into the variable on the left. To COMPARE use == .
